title: API Architecture at a Glance

tldr.In one line: A production API is a layered system — client, edge, gateway, application, then data and AI layers — and you add each layer only when a real problem demands it.
tldr.In plain English: Picture an airport: check-in, security and the gate each do one job before you board. A request travels the same way. A CDN may answer straight away, a gateway checks who you are, and the app does the real work with a database or an AI model behind it.
tldr.You'll be able to: Name the main layers of a production API and the job of each · Trace which layers a read, a write and an AI chat request pass through · Decide when a layer is worth adding and when it is just extra complexity

takeaways: Production APIs are layered systems: edge → gateway → application → data/AI.
Not every API needs every layer — add complexity when the problem demands it.
AI systems introduce a new layer (the AI gateway) with different failure and cost characteristics than a typical database call.
This map will be referenced constantly — bookmark [Part 18](../18-production-architecture/README.md) for the full version.
quiz: 1. What is the difference between the API gateway layer and the application service layer?
2. Why not add a CDN, a gateway, a queue and a cache to every new API from day one?
